body:
This extension depends on `XR_VARJO_quad_views` also being enabled, so, we can't have this one by itself - that actually breaks initializing OpenXR on Android XR.

Perhaps this should be moved up into the `if (p_version < XR_API_VERSION_1_1_0)`? Or, maybe that `if` should be removed entirely if this is needed on Varjo even when using OpenXR 1.1?

Yeah that was the part I was discussing with Varjo. Since `XR_VARJO_quad_views` no longer is needed with OpenXR 1.1, the dependency seems to be weird. Hence the comment around this.

I think `XR_VARJO_foveated_rendering` needs a spec change so it no longer needs `XR_VARJO_quad_views` when running OpenXR 1.1

Until then, I guess we need to enable `XR_VARJO_quad_views` in OpenXR 1.1 and hope that doesn't break things on any platform that doesn't want duplicate behaviour (like we've had with PICO on a number of other mutually exclusive extensions they support).

For Android XR, we don't need to enable either of these extensions when using OpenXR 1.1 (although, it does support them and we could use them with OpenXR 1.0).

Could we maybe have this check if the `xr/openxr/view_configuration` is set to "Stereo with Foveated Inset", and if not, don't attempt to load these extensions?

Because I don't think we support changing the view configuration at runtime, right? So this would have to be configured in project settings if the developer intended to use this. And then folks could explicitly disable it for any platforms that had issues (avoiding another issue like the Pico one with eye tracking)
